Explore the fountain

0 / 3details discovered

The sundial

A sundial crowns the upper basin. Look for its shadow: the fountain keeps time in more ways than one.

The stepped basins

These granite cascades echo Chicago’s continental divide, where waterways part toward different oceans.

The water cannon

The nozzle launches water across the river. Its arc echoes Chicago’s movable bridges—built from water instead of steel.

The Nicholas J. Melas Centennial Fountain

Dedicated in 1989 to mark the water district’s centennial, the fountain was designed by Dirk Lohan of Lohan Associates. Its stepped cascades, sundial and water cannon stand in River Esplanade Park, at N McClurg Court and E River Drive on the north bank of the Chicago River, Chicago, Illinois.

Stone, water and a century of history

The fountain honors former MWRD president Nicholas J. Melas. Explore its details above, then read the Chicago Architecture Center’s history and the architect’s account of the design.

The story behind the fountain
1989

A centennial gift

Dedicated to the water district’s first 100 years, from its founding in 1889.

Dirk Lohan

Lohan Associates designed the meeting of stone, falling water and a river-spanning arc.

Nicholas J. Melas

The fountain honors the longtime water district leader whose name it carries.
